title: Sneaker Customizer with Save/Load State
prompt:
Create a single HTML file implementing a 3D sneaker customizer using Three.js. Since we don't have a sneaker model, load 'WaterBottle.glb' using GLTFLoader as a stand-in product model that the user can customize.

SCENE SETUP:
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 1.5, 3) looking at origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.5) and a directional light at (5, 5, 5) with intensity 1.0.
- Set background color to #1a1a2e.
- Load 'WaterBottle.glb' using GLTFLoader from CDN (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js). Center and scale the model so it fits nicely (auto-scale to bounding box ~1.5 units).
- Add OrbitControls for camera rotation.
- Add a subtle grid helper on the ground plane.

CUSTOMIZATION SYSTEM:
The model has multiple mesh children. Identify up to 5 mesh parts from the loaded model. Each part can be independently colored. Track parts as 'part0' through 'part4'.

UI ELEMENTS (DOM overlay):
1. A part selector panel on the left with buttons labeled 'Part 0' through 'Part 4' (id='btn-part-0' through 'btn-part-4'). The currently selected part button should have class 'active'.
2. A color palette on the right with 6 color swatches: #ff0000 (Red), #00ff00 (Green), #0000ff (Blue), #ffff00 (Yellow), #ff00ff (Magenta), #ffffff (White). Each swatch is a button with id='color-{hex without #}' (e.g., 'color-ff0000').
3. A 'Save State' button (id='btn-save') that serializes the current color configuration to localStorage key 'sneaker_config'.
4. A 'Load State' button (id='btn-load') that restores colors from localStorage.
5. A 'Reset' button (id='btn-reset') that resets all parts to white (#ffffff).
6. A 'Rotate Toggle' button (id='btn-rotate') that toggles auto-rotation of the model (default: off, rotation speed 0.01 rad/frame around Y).
7. A status bar at the bottom (id='status-bar') showing the last action performed (e.g., 'Saved configuration', 'Loaded configuration', 'Reset to defaults', 'Color applied: #ff0000 to Part 2').

STATE MANAGEMENT:
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields:
- modelLoaded: boolean, true once GLB is fully loaded
- selectedPart: number (0-4), default 0
- partColors: array of 5 hex strings, default all '#ffffff'
- autoRotate: boolean, default false
- rotationAngle: number, cumulative Y rotation in radians
- savedConfig: string or null, the JSON string last saved to localStorage
- lastAction: string, description of last user action
- cameraDistance: number, distance from camera to origin
- meshCount: number, total mesh children found in the model
- partsAvailable: number, min(meshCount, 5) - actual customizable parts

INTERACTION DETAILS:
- Clicking a part button sets selectedPart to that index and highlights the corresponding mesh with a subtle outline or emissive boost.
- Clicking a color swatch applies that color to the currently selected part's material.color and updates partColors array.
- Save serializes partColors to JSON and stores in localStorage under 'sneaker_config'. Also updates savedConfig.
- Load reads from localStorage, parses JSON, applies colors to all parts. If no saved config exists, status shows 'No saved configuration found'.
- Reset sets all part colors to #ffffff and applies to materials.
- Auto-rotate toggles model spinning. The button text changes to 'Stop Rotation' when active, 'Rotate Toggle' when inactive.

ANIMATION LOOP:
- Update rotationAngle when autoRotate is true.
- Keep cameraDistance updated each frame.
- Render scene each frame.

Style the UI with a dark theme, semi-transparent panels, and clean typography.
physics_constraints: No physics simulation required. Camera distance must remain positive and finite. Rotation angle must increment monotonically when auto-rotate is on. All color values must be valid hex strings.
